Concerns about national security triggered a debate on banning the app almost six years ago. To address those concerns, an agreement to create a TikTok US joint venture was reached between Washington and Beijing. A number of US investors will now be in control of the newly formed entity. author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Russian political scientist Andrey Kortunov has told Al Jazeera that both Russia and Ukraine want to convince the US they are “not an obstacle to peace”, but that Moscow knows time is on its side as it makes slow but steady military advances.

“Definitely here in Moscow they would prefer to find a diplomatic answer … but I think the perception in Moscow is that time is on the Russian side, and therefore, the negotiating position of Ukraine is not likely to get any better anytime soon,” said Kortunov, who previously served as director general of the Russian International Affairs Council.

Kortunov said Moscow expects its battlefield gains to continue if no settlement is reached. However, he said he believes there is some room for negotiation on territory, with Russia potentially keeping control of some adjacent Ukrainian areas and then offering “minor” land swaps.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Donald Trump’s latest attempt to seize Greenland shows that the president is willing to use US force to determine international borders, even at the expense of sovereignty.

Western allies - NATO countries included -  publicly formed a united front, but private messages have revealed a more deferential approach to dealing with Trump.

This latest crisis may have been averted, but the question remains: Does the so-called rules-based international order apply to Trump?

Contributors: 
Louise Bokkenheuser - Writer and editor
Branko Marcetic - Staff writer, Jacobin
Anchal Vohra - Columnist, Foreign Policy
Ulrich Bruckner - Professor for European studies, Stanford University

On our radar:

Donald Trump launched his highly-publicised "Board of Peace" initiative at the World Economic Forum in Davos this week.

The signing ceremony followed a familiar pattern for this White House - a carefully staged event centred on Trump, his overblown claims of peacemaking, and speeches in praise of him.
title: How far will Trump’s imperial ambition go? | The Listening Post
